thread:
inc-bot: INCIDENT CREATED: routing anomaly detected for inference-api. Multiple regions reporting rapid health-check flips causing cross-region routing churn (us-east <-> us-west <-> eu). Alert window started 2026-03-15T11:02:00Z. PagerDuty: P2 -> paging oncall.

maria: i'm paged — jumping in. what services are affected? any customer-facing errors? :eyes:

oncall-sre: getting telemetry now. traces show same request ids bouncing regions, 503s spike for ~60s bursts.

rajesh: quick summary from runtime side — health-check agent is flapping on a small subset of nodes in eu due to a combination of aggressive probe retries and a routing policy that immediately favors lower-latency variants. when eu briefly reports healthy, traffic shifts there, then a scheduled maintenance probe hits and marks it unhealthy, so traffic moves to us-west, rinse/repeat. looks like a saw-tooth but more like a waltz :)

rajesh: logs snippet:
```
[11:01:58] eu-node-12 health_check: PASS (rtt=18ms)
[11:01:59] routing: re-route to eu (policy=latency-first)
[11:02:12] eu-node-12 health_check: FAIL (timeout)
[11:02:12] routing: re-route to us-west (policy=latency-first)
[11:02:28] us-west-node-03 health_check: PASS
[11:02:30] eu-node-12 health_check: PASS
```

maria: confirmed. customer-visible 503s and latency spikes. sam — any customer reports?

sam: ACME-App reported elevated errors and increased cost (they retried aggressively). support ticket #9872 opened, customer saw ~15% request failures for ~9 minutes. forwarding details to their SE.

eli: assigning impacts — is this causing failed inferences or just higher latency/errors? need to know for outward comms.

zoe: both. some requests hit fallback model variants (smaller quantized variant) which caused degraded output for a subset of calls. not catastrophic but noticeable for users.

rajesh: immediate mitigation plan: 1) disable "latency-first" smart routing temporarily so we stop bouncing; 2) pin routing to current stable model-variant for the customer-facing pool; 3) increase health-check grace and widen probe cooldown so transient probe jitter doesn't flip state.

oncall-sre: i'm going to mute pager alerts for this signal to avoid noise during mitigation.

maria: agreed. can someone run the config change? i don't want to redeploy runtime code during this.

deploy-bot: command queued by rajesh: `redwoodctl routing set-policy --scope=global --policy=prefer-stable --reason="mitigate probe-waltz"`

rajesh: running now — patching in prod config: 
```bash
redwoodctl routing update --policy latency-first --enabled=false --dry-run=false
redwoodctl route pin --selector=customer:acme-app --variant=stable-v1
redwoodctl healthcheck update --grace-seconds=20 --cooldown-ms=45000
```

deploy-bot: succeeded — global policy latency-first disabled. route pinned for acme-app to stable-v1. healthcheck config updated.

oncall-sre: seeing immediate reduction in re-routes. eu stable node remains in place, 503s dropping. latency back to baseline within ~2 min. :thumbsup:

sam: confirmed ACME ticket update — error rate down to normal, they're unblocked. SE is asking for a short incident summary.

eli: good. we should still root-cause the probe jitter. rajesh, can we reproduce in staging with the same probe cadence?

rajesh: yes — I reproduced locally with a synthetic probe that has a 200ms jitter + aggressive retry window. root cause is twofold: a) probe agent had a recent tweak to lower timeout thresholds for faster failover; b) routing policy laddered variants with no cooldown so it reacted to a single PASS. combined these created oscillation.

zoe: action items:
- revert the probe timeout change or set it behind a feature flag (owner: rajesh)
- add a routing cooldown parameter and require N successive PASS/FAIL before region switch (owner: eng-runtime)
- add per-customer pinning grace for model variant switch during health flaps (owner: product)
- postmortem and customer communication (owner: eli)

maria: i'll create the incident in incident tracker and set the severity to P2 with timeline.

inc-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigation applied (policy disabled, variant pinned, healthcheck tuned) at 2026-03-15T11:10:22Z. Status: recovering.

rajesh: started a small staging patch to require 3 consecutive health_check PASS before re-route, will roll to prod in canary later today.

deploy-bot: canary deployment queued — target: eng-runtime-canary (10%)

oncall-sre: monitoring for 30m — will escalate if re-routes resume.

eli: thanks everyone. quick comms note for support: send ACME a short summary and offer a 1:1 to review retry/backoff settings.

maria: closing pager for this signal. tagging for postmortem: `investigate-probe-waltz-routing`.

zoe: postmortem draft action items and owner list in #postmortems in ~24h.

sam: ACME responded: "Thanks — good follow-up, appreciate the quick turnaround." :white_check_mark:

maria: incident resolved. moving to monitoring state. follow-ups scheduled.
